campaign.title: LEO National Emergency Failover Study

protocol.title: LEO National Emergency Failover Study
protocol.primary_claim: Table 1 six-country optimistic downlink capacity and fraction of lost cable capacity
protocol.primary_configuration: Released five-shell idealized TLEs, 198 gateways, Config A, 200000 requested terminals, uncapped paper GCB, coordinated RF, maximum flow, no incumbent demand
protocol.sampling: 15 consecutive one-second snapshots from the artifact TLE epoch, plus sensitivity at 6/12/18 hours. These are deterministic model states, not independent replications.
protocol.comparison_rule: Report signed relative difference from Table 1; within 5% is numerical agreement under this protocol, not statistical proof. Outside 5% is a discrepancy in this implementation, not disproof of real satellite capacity.
protocol.uncertainty: Report time-state minimum, maximum and mean. Do not bootstrap seconds or report inferential confidence intervals; input/model uncertainty is not quantified by deterministic repeat execution.
protocol.ablations: Population placement; GCB cap 0/1000/10000/100000; demand/fairness beam policies; released-vs-paper GCB semantics; Config B Ku sensitivity; 2.5-Gbps Ku sensitivity; idealized constellation growth under uniform deployment.
corrections: Use correct shell cumulative offsets for range thresholds; released graph generator does not advance its cumulative offset after shell 1.
Use second*1e9 graph timestamps consistently; released flow generator uses second*1e10.
Paper variant uses Algorithm 1 batch of 200 and redistributes residual terminals among eligible cells, including empty cells with cap zero.

Artifact variant retains batch floor(80*Ku), excludes empty cells, and leaves surplus terminals unallocated for positive caps. Density placement uses exact-budget Hamilton apportionment to avoid released rounding overshoot.
Spatial pruning uses a 100-km margin and exact upstream PyEphem ranges; first/last country cells are exhaustively audited at every epoch.
Omit global incumbent cell nodes only for no-incumbent experiments; those nodes do not affect routing or country beam mapping.
Use maximum flow for aggregate capacity. Cost minimization affects routing/utilization and is not used to infer published ISL utilization.
Remap beams for each orbital snapshot rather than silently using stale t=0 demands. This is a documented deviation from the released 15-second routing loop.
not_reproduced_by_primary_design: Live Starlink measurements or physical emergency deployment
Original Calypso/RIPE Atlas cable rankings or proprietary TeleGeography capacity derivation
Incumbent-traffic maps, hot-potato routing, gateway sovereignty restrictions and ISL/gateway utilization figures
Joint Config C constellation and link upgrade: 2.5 Gbps here changes Ku on the baseline constellation only
limitations: Upper-bound model assumes maximum link rates, clear line of sight, fully utilized terminals, functioning gateways and no competing traffic.
Released beam heuristic is reused; it does not prove optimal spectrum allocation.
Cable design/lit capacity is not observed national traffic lost; Lithuania uses an older per-user-bandwidth proxy.
Short orbital window and three sensitivity epochs do not establish long-term availability.
Artifact reproduction is not independent empirical validation. No weather, terrain, inter-satellite/constellation RF interference or deployment logistics are modeled.

Post-execution clarification: released code doubles ISL rates when Ku=2.5 Gbps. The original frozen protocol described this as Ku-only; the amended interpretation is a Ku+ISL sensitivity, with baseline Ka and constellation. The frozen document remains unchanged for audit.
Literature review is recorded source by source; inaccessible or unread sources are not treated as reviewed.
Primary execution preceded completion of the supporting bibliography review; later review does not retrospectively alter its predeclared configurations.

Published Table 1 arithmetic inconsistency: Lithuania prints 2,005 Gbps satellite capacity, 101 Gbps lost cable capacity and 198 percent. Dividing the printed capacities gives 1,985.15 percent. Recorded capacity/cable fractions use the printed capacity denominator; no source field is silently corrected.

provenance.execution: local CPU simulation, no AWS satellite test infrastructure
provenance.graph_generation: Exact PyEphem distances after conservative spatial pruning; two exhaustive cell audits per country/epoch
provenance.protocol_clarification: Ku=2.5 invokes doubled ISLs, unchanged Ka; original protocol retained.
provenance.epoch_interpretation: Generated idealized TLE epoch, not the wall-clock date of execution or a measured operational constellation.
